chunks: Al-Shaykh informed me from Abū al-Qāsim Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Yaʿqūb, from ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Qāsim al-Khazzāz, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Kathīr, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: its like.

He said: While Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام was one day sitting with Ibn al-Ḥanafiyyah, he said to him: O Muḥammad, bring me a vessel of water so that I may perform wudu (ablution) for salat (prayer). Muḥammad brought him the water, and he poured it with his left hand onto his right hand, then he said: In the Name of Allah, and praise belongs to Allah who made water purifying and did not make it impure.

He said: Then he performed istinjāʾ and said: O Allah, fortify my private part, keep it chaste, conceal my nakedness, and forbid me to the Fire. He said: Then he rinsed his mouth and said: O Allah, prompt me with my proof on the day I meet You, and loosen my tongue with Your remembrance. Then he drew water into his nose and said: O Allah, do not forbid me the fragrance of jannah (paradise), and make me among those who smell its fragrance, its comfort, and its perfume. He said: Then he washed his face and said: O Allah, whiten my face on the day when faces will be blackened, and do not blacken my face on the day when faces will be whitened. Then he washed his right hand and said: O Allah, give me my book in my right hand, and everlastingness in the gardens in my left, and call me to account...

Then he washed his left hand and said: O Allah, do not give me my book in my left hand, do not make it chained to my neck, and I seek refuge in You from the severing punishments of the fires. Then he wiped his head and said: O Allah, cover me with Your mercy and Your blessings. Then he wiped his feet and said: O Allah, make me firm upon the ṣirāṭ on the day when feet will slip, and make my striving in that which pleases You with me. Then he raised his head and looked at Muḥammad and said: O Muḥammad, whoever performs wudu (ablution) like my wudu and says the like of what I have said, Allah creates for him from every drop an angel who sanctifies Him, glorifies Him, and magnifies Him, and Allah writes for him the reward of that until the Day of Judgment.

As for what is contained in the Shaykh’s words—may Allah Most High support him—regarding the limit of the face in wudu (ablution), and that it is from the hairline to the lower end of the beard hair, and that over which the thumb and middle finger pass, what indicates it is that what we considered is that concerning which there is no disagreement that it is part of the face. As for what exceeds that, it is differed over, so we adopted what the Ummah agreed upon and left what they differed about. No one may say that the face is whatever a human being faces with, because that would require that the ears be part of the face, and the chest be part of the face, and every limb with which a human being faces be part of the face; and this is invalid without disagreement. This too indicates it.

key_terms.حِسَابًا يَسِيرًا: an easy reckoning on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.طَهُورًا: purifying; describing water as ritually cleansing
key_terms.ٱسْتَنْجَى: he performed istinjāʾ, cleansing oneself after relieving oneself
key_terms.ٱلصِّرَاطِ: the bridge/path on which firmness is sought on the Day of Judgment
key_terms.ٱلْجَنَّةِ: jannah (paradise), invoked in supplication for its fragrance and reward
key_terms.ٱلْقِيَامَةِ: the Day of Judgment, the final resurrection and reckoning
key_terms.ٱلْوَجْهِ: the face, here in the legal sense of the area to be washed in wudu
key_terms.ٱلْوُضُوءِ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification before salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: What supplications are recited during the wudu of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, and what is the defined boundary of the face in wudu?
ai.summary: This report describes the wudu (ablution) of Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام together with the supplications recited at each step, linking ritual purification with remembrance of Allah and preparation for the afterlife. It also concludes with a juristic clarification regarding the boundary of the face in wudu, emphasizing what is agreed upon in defining the obligatory area to be washed.
